hero.filename: Jarre à provisions Tepe Gyan IV.jpg
hero.title: File:Jarre à provisions Tepe Gyan IV.jpg
hero.source: Jarre à provisions Tepe Gyan IV
hero.description: Mainly known for a necropolis of 19 graves, the phase of Giyan IV delivers ceramic in abundance. The jars are generally decorated with raised bands in horizontal and wavy raised bands. Only the neck of the jar is painted, the rest is blank. The most significant motifs in this phase are pairs of birds with wings spread in the shape of a comb and rows of sawtooth patterns.
categories: Author died more than 100 years ago public domain images
Collection from Near East and Iran, Jubilee Park Museum

gallery.title: File:Iranian - Small Jar with Birds, Rosettes, and Geometric Patterns - Walters 482395.jpg
gallery.description: The simplicity of this design is characteristic of the painted pottery from the site of Tepe Giyan in western Iran. The birds may represent ostriches. Such pottery has been found in burials along with jewelry and weapons.
